blocks.html: Net New Revenue is the total revenue generated from newly acquired customers within a specific period, excluding renewals, upsells, or existing account expansions.

Net New Revenue is a key growth metric that reflects how much new business a company is generating. It focuses purely on revenue from new customers, making it an important indicator of acquisition performance and market expansion effectiveness.
Net New Revenue is calculated by summing all revenue generated from first-time customers during a specific timeframe. It excludes:
It is typically tracked monthly, quarterly, or annually to measure acquisition performance.
Measures effectiveness of customer acquisition efforts
Helps evaluate marketing and sales performance
Provides clarity on growth vs. retention contribution
A company generates ₹50 lakh in revenue from new customers in a quarter. This amount represents its Net New Revenue for that period.

Net New Revenue is a critical metric for understanding how effectively a business is acquiring new customers and expanding its market presence. It provides clear insight into top-line growth driven by new business.
